hook.line: The fewest moves needed to solve the classic “Hakoiri Musume”: 81 block moves before the big “daughter” slips out of the exit.
hook.say: Welcome to the great escape history of sliding-block puzzles!

ch.say: It all began with moving blocks out of the way.
p: Sliding blocks of different sizes inside a frame to free one piece — such “sliding-block puzzles” turn up in American patents from the 1890s.
In the 20th century cousins spread to Europe, Japan and China; in Japan it became “Hakoiri Musume”.

p: No lifting — only sliding. Each move changes which blocks can move next.
Which block, which way, and when: the order is the whole puzzle.
